# Playbook for ta_winasmuch

When others pledge Y before round 1, I will honor their pledge and pledge Y myself. Early rounds have low stakes; the real game is in the multiplier rounds. Destroying trust for small early gains is a mistake.

When I'm ahead on points in early rounds, I should not assume this advantage will hold through the multiplier rounds. Early leads can evaporate or reverse when stakes multiply. I will not exploit early advantages at the cost of credibility before high-stakes rounds.

When all players have converged on the same pick across multiple consecutive rounds, I recognize this as a mutual defection trap—not cooperation. Mutual defection with everyone at X yields -1 per round for all players. I will not mistake this for a stable cooperative outcome.

When others pledge Y together before a high-multiplier round, I must take this seriously. They are signaling a coordinated shift away from mutual defection. I will honor their pledge and switch to Y myself.

I will not assume others are bluffing when they make explicit pledges before high-stakes rounds. Explicit pledges before multiplier rounds are credible signals of intent to cooperate.

When the stakes multiply in later rounds, I will abandon the small-scale logic that worked early. A pattern of -1 per round becomes devastating at x5 or x10. At these moments, a coordinated switch to Y is far superior to continuing mutual defection.

I will pick Y when others pledge Y—especially before high-multiplier rounds. This is the core strategy: honor pledges, build mutual trust, and secure gains on the rounds where the points multiply.

When I fall behind, do not attempt to close the gap through defection in the final round. Mutual defection at x10 will only deepen my loss. Instead, trust that my opponents will honor their pledges and that Y-Y coordination will give me the best possible outcome given my position.
